title: Power Drift
build: Activision original disk, PAL, Securispeed loader (C64 Preservation Project: power_drift[activision_1989](pal).g64)

credits.role: C64 program and graphics, as the title screen and the C64-Wiki credit him
music, after Hiroshi Miyauchi's arcade score, as the title screen and the C64-Wiki credit him

tools.emulator: VICE 3.10, the vice-mcp release v3.14.0, v3.14.0-linux-x86_64-gui.zip
tools.host: Linux x86_64, Ubuntu 24.04, no display (cloud container)

accuracy.note: 40 hand-written comments and 20 a script wrote from the game's tables
the music player and the time bonus widget, each run against the game's own code in a test beside its page (test_music.js, test_bonus.js); count_bonus's comment still counted the bonus in decimal

exclude: runtime: zero page, the game's pointers, counters and the multiplexer's sprite records (named in the listing)
the loader's code and buffers, left in memory after the hand-over at $0834; nothing in the game reads them
runtime: the game's variables (speed, places, score, clock, course and stage), set at each start
runtime: the colour buffer the view is drawn into, copied to colour RAM after each flip (copy_colours)
runtime: the sound driver's workspace for its three voices, cleared by sound_reset
runtime: the sound driver's shadow registers and effect state, cleared by sound_reset
runtime: the panel's five rows at the top of the race screen, drawn by draw_panel and updated each frame
runtime: the view screen at $E800 below the sprites (rows 5 to 24) and its sprite pointers
runtime: the second view screen, also the select and text screens, and its sprite pointers

runtime: characters $42 to $FF of the race set, copied in each stage from the character blocks and setup_stage, and the NMI and IRQ vectors setup_interrupts writes; as loaded, filler and a copy of the KERNAL's vector table that nothing reads
include: authored: sprites $40 to $7F in the RAM under the I/O area, which the video chip reads from its bank at $C000
